title: Weight initialisation by layer type
description: Walks over every submodule and initialises it according to its type: He-normal for convolutions (ReLU network), identity affine transform for batch norm, and Glorot-uniform for the final linear layer.
hints: Different layer types need different schemes; ReLU networks use a gain-corrected variance.
nn.init.kaiming_normal_ for convs; nn.init.xavier_*_ for the classifier.
nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode="fan_out", nonlinearity="relu") and nn.init.xavier_uniform_(m.weight).
explanation: Kaiming init scales the variance by 2/fan so that ReLU activations keep their magnitude through depth. BatchNorm starts as the identity (gamma=1, beta=0).

title: Clipping at the wrong moment
description: Mini-batch update with gradient-norm clipping to stabilise training: gradients are computed first, rescaled if their global norm is too large, and only then applied.
code:
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
logits = model(images)
loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)
grad_norm = nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=max_grad_norm)
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()

errors.explanation: Clipping runs before backward(), so there are no fresh gradients to rescale (.grad is empty or stale). backward() has to come first.
clip_grad_norm_ belongs after backward() (gradients exist) and before step() (so the update uses the clipped values).

hints: Two adjacent lines are in the wrong order.
What must exist before clip_grad_norm_ can act?
backward() first, then clip_grad_norm_, then step().

title: Validation loop
description: Computes sample-weighted loss and accuracy of a model on a loader, in inference mode and without building gradients.
code:
@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate(model, loader, device):
    model.train()
    loss_sum, correct, n = 0.0, 0, 0
    for x, y in loader:
        x = x.to(device)
        y = y.to(device)
        logits = model(x)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, y)
        b = x.shape[0]
        loss_sum += loss.item()
        correct += (logits.argmax(dim=0) == y).sum().item()
        n += b
    return {"loss": loss_sum / n, "acc": correct / n}

errors.explanation: BatchNorm must use its running statistics (and dropout be off) during evaluation: call eval().
cross_entropy returns a batch mean; multiply by the batch size before accumulating so the final division by n is a true average.
logits are (batch, classes); the predicted class is the arg-max over dim 1, not over the batch axis.

hints: Three independent mistakes: mode, loss accumulation, prediction.
Check each of lines 3, 11 and 12 against what BatchNorm, mean-reduction and the (B, K) logits shape require.
model.eval(); loss.item() * b; argmax(dim=1).
